title: Waves and the Electromagnetic Spectrum
seo_title: Year 11 Science: Waves and the Electromagnetic Spectrum Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_text: Transverse and longitudinal waves; properties of waves (amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period) and the wave equation; measuring wave speed; the electromagnetic spectrum; properties and uses of electromagnetic waves; hazards of ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays; (higher tier) refraction.
meta_desc: Free Year 11 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on waves: transverse and longitudinal waves, v = fλ, period, the electromagnetic spectrum, uses and hazards of EM waves and refraction. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Radio waves have the longest wavelength; gamma rays the shortest.
body_html:
How to think about it

Waves transfer energy without moving matter along.

  • Transverse waves vibrate at right angles to the direction of travel; longitudinal waves (sound) vibrate along it.
  • v = fλ and T = 1 ÷ f.
  • Electromagnetic spectrum: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma. All travel at 3 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.
Example

f = 50 Hz, λ = 2 m. Speed?

v = fλ = 50 × 2

Answer: 100 m/s

Example

Which is longer: microwaves or X-rays?

Radio end is longer

Answer: microwaves

Common mistakes

  • Thinking sound is transverse.
  • Thinking radio waves are faster than light in a vacuum.
  • Thinking the water moves along with the wave.

faq.a: Wave speed = frequency × wavelength (v = fλ). Speed in m/s, frequency in Hz and wavelength in m.

faq.q: What is the order of the electromagnetic spectrum?
faq.a: Radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays. Wavelength decreases and frequency increases along this list.
Ultraviolet can damage skin. X-rays and gamma rays are ionising and can cause mutations and cancer.
